info.name: Seismic DMS (SDMS) - Single File Restore Test Collection (clean-room)
info.description:
Swagger-driven + repo-mined test collection for the SDMS single-file point-in-time restore feature. Spec: OSDU-Seismic-DDMS/app/sdms/docs/api/openapi.yaml (Seismic DMS Service v3.0.0, base /seistore-svc/api/v3). Endpoints under test: POST /operation/restore, GET /operation/restore/{operationId}. Source mined statically (never executed) from app/sdms/src/services/operation (handler.ts, service.ts, restore-status.ts) + shared/error.ts, shared/featureflags.ts. Full analysis: seismic-restore.spec-vs-code.md.

TEST-PLAN COVERAGE (references/seismic-single-file-restore-test-plan.md):
- Functional: TC-RST-FUNC-01/02 (update-then-restore, uniform/dataset), TC-RST-FUNC-03/04 (delete-then-restore) - see 'EXECUTION - FUNCTIONAL SCENARIOS'.
- Validation: TC-RST-VLD-01..08. Auth: TC-RST-AUTH-01..04. Concurrency: TC-RST-CON-01 (deterministic 409) / CON-02 (other partition). Status: TC-RST-STS-01..05. Feature flag: TC-RST-FLG-01.
- TC-RST-REL-01/02 (dependency-outage) are infrastructure fault-injection scenarios that cannot be provoked from an API collection; run them manually with a fault harness (documented, not scripted).

KEY REPO-CONFIRMED behaviour [confirmed: repo]:
(1) POST 202 body is { operation_id, statusUrl } (snake_case, NO status field) - unlike swagger RestoreAccepted; RST-001's 'status=InProgress' in the trigger response is NOT met by code. Capture is defensive.
(2) POST also returns 404 (dataset missing), 423 (write-locked), 503 (retention SDMS_RESTORE_MAX_DAYS unconfigured / Redis down) - none documented on the POST.
(3) Concurrency 409 is per DATA PARTITION / tenant, NOT per dataset (RestoreOperationLock + Cosmos query keyed by tenant).
(4) GET status: missing data-partition-id -> 400 (not 403); unknown/malformed id -> 404.
(5) Terminal statuses Succeeded/Failed; in-flight InProgress. Failure detail is in error_message (swagger calls it 'error').
(6) Feature gate FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_RESTORE off -> 403 (checkFeature runs before body validation). POST needs subproject.admin; GET needs a registered partition user.
(7) LIMITATION: restoring a DELETED dataset returns 404 - restorePush gates on current dataset-metadata existence (createDataset sets dataset.name for a dataset-level sdPath). So RST-010 / TC-RST-FUNC-03/04 as written are NOT satisfiable via POST /operation/restore against current code; the test documents this.

RUN NOTES: set base_url host, access_token (subproject.admin), tenant_esd/tenant_default_acls before running. Set a per-request delay (~poll_delay_ms) in the runner for the poll steps. RST-011 access-policy parity is covered in a single run: SETUP provisions BOTH a uniform and an access_policy=dataset subproject/dataset (Setup 2b/3b/5b/6b/7b, sharing one legal tag), the dedicated 'EXECUTION - FUNCTIONAL SCENARIOS (DATASET POLICY)' folder runs FUNC-02/04 against the *_ds variable namespace, and CLEANUP tears both down (Cleanup 1b/2b). The dataset-policy restore role is dataset.admin - the same access_token must carry it. SDMS uses sd:// path addressing + ltag header, NOT the OSDU acl/legal request envelope (seismic.md S2).

item.name: PRECHECK - Restore feature-flag gate
PRECHECK - probe restore feature flag (skip whole collection if disabled)

exec: // Probe the GET status endpoint with a dummy operation id to detect whether the restore feature is enabled.
// [confirmed: repo] checkFeature runs before the lookup: FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_RESTORE off -> 403 'feature is not enabled'.
// When the feature is ON, an unknown operation id resolves to 404.
// Feature disabled: nothing has been provisioned yet, so stop the run entirely (skips SETUP/EXECUTION/CLEANUP).
pm.test('SKIP: restore feature is disabled - skipping the entire collection', function () { pm.expect(true).to.be.true; });
console.log('[PRECHECK] Restore feature is DISABLED (403 feature is not enabled). Skipping the entire collection.');
// Feature enabled: unknown operation id yields 404. Proceed with the rest of the collection.
pm.test('restore feature enabled (GET status returns 404 for an unknown operation id)', function () { pm.expect(code).to.eql(404); });
// Anything else is inconclusive (e.g. auth/registration issue) - surface it rather than silently continuing.
pm.test('PRECHECK inconclusive - expected 404 (enabled) or 403 feature-not-enabled (disabled), got ' + code, function () { pm.expect([403, 404]).to.include(code); });

request.description: Feature-flag gate. GET /operation/restore/{operationId} with a dummy operation id. [confirmed: repo] checkFeature runs first: if FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_RESTORE is off the service returns 403 with a 'feature is not enabled' message and the whole collection is skipped (setNextRequest(null)); if enabled, an unknown id returns 404 and the run proceeds.

item.name: EXECUTION - CONTRACT & NEGATIVES
RST-001 / TC-RST-AUTH-04 - POST restore (happy path, capture operation_id)

exec: // Reset any operationId captured by a previous restore so a failed POST can't leave a stale id for the poll.
// restorePointInTime must be AFTER dataset creation, IN THE PAST, and within retention.
// The SETUP dataset was just created, so 'now' is the only safe point after creation; back off 2s to stay in the past.
var j = {}; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {}
// [confirmed: repo] handler returns { operation_id, statusUrl } (snake_case, no 'status'). Capture defensively.
// NOTE (spec-vs-code): swagger RestoreAccepted also declares status:'InProgress' but code omits it; RST-001 asserts InProgress via the status endpoint instead.

request.description: POST /operation/restore. RestoreRequest requires sdPath, restorePointInTime. Role: subproject.admin. 202 -> RestoreAccepted. Holds the per-partition restore lock until it completes (drained by the poll below).

item.name: TC-RST-CON-01 / RST-007 - POST restore while op1 in progress -> 409 (deterministic, per data partition)

exec: // [confirmed: repo] concurrency is scoped per DATA PARTITION/tenant. op1 (previous request) is still in progress,
// so this second trigger in the same partition must be rejected with 409 - even for the same/other dataset.
pm.test('conflict 409 (restore already in progress)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(409); });
pm.test('409 message names an in-progress operation', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/already in progress/i); });

request.description: [confirmed: repo] RestoreOperationLock (Redis) + Cosmos in-progress query, both keyed by tenant, throw ALREADY_EXISTS(409). Runs immediately after the happy-path 202 (op1 still InProgress) so the 409 is deterministic. This request is REJECTED, so it starts no new operation and leaks no lock.

item.name: RST-002 / RST-003 / TC-RST-STS-01 - GET status (poll op1 to terminal, expect Succeeded)

exec: // Wait between polls (10s by default) so we don't hammer the status endpoint. Skips the delay on the first poll.
// Stop polling on an unexpected status code - don't burn retries; fall through to the next request.
var j = {}; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {}
pm.test('TC-RST-STS-01 required status fields present', function () {
pm.expect.fail('Restore terminated as Failed: ' + (j.error_message || j.error || 'no detail'));
// [confirmed: repo] Rejected is a terminal status. The FIRST restore triggered in this collection has no
// prior version to revert to, so it transitions to Rejected with a message containing 'nothing to restore'.
var rejMsg = (j.error_message || j.error || j.message || j.statusMessage || pm.response.text() || '');
pm.test('RST-003 first restore Rejected (nothing to restore)', function () { pm.expect(status).to.eql('Rejected'); pm.expect(rejMsg).to.match(/nothing to restore/i); });
else { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', '0'); pm.expect.fail('Restore not terminal within ' + maxAttempts + ' polls (last: ' + status + ')'); }

request.description: GET /operation/restore/{operationId}. Polls status until terminal (Succeeded/Failed/Rejected), draining op1's per-partition lock. The first restore in this collection has no prior version to revert to, so it terminates as Rejected with a 'nothing to restore' message (asserted here). Configure a per-request delay (~poll_delay_ms) in the runner. Also covers TC-RST-STS-01 (200 + required fields).

request.description: [confirmed: repo] restoreAt <= created_date -> 400 'restorePointInTime must be after the dataset creation time ...'. Assumes SETUP created the dataset in the last ~2h.

item.name: TC-RST-VLD-08 - POST restore timestamp when dataset did not exist yet -> 400

exec: pm.test('rejected 400 (dataset did not exist at timestamp)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(400); });

request.description: [confirmed: repo] The spec lists 'Dataset did not exist at the provided timestamp' as a distinct 400, but the code enforces it via the SAME created_date guard as VLD-07 (restoreAt <= created_date -> 400). This case uses a timestamp ~6h in the past (before the freshly-created dataset) to exercise that guard from the 'did-not-exist' angle.

item.name: TC-RST-FLG-01 - POST restore feature-flag gate (403 if disabled / 400 if enabled)

exec: // [confirmed: repo] checkFeature(Feature.RESTORE) runs BEFORE body validation. Sending an invalid body means:
//   feature OFF -> 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; feature ON -> 400 (validation) - and never starts a restore.
pm.test('403 when restore feature disabled, else 400 (feature on)', function () { pm.expect([400, 403]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 403) { pm.test('403 body mentions feature not enabled', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/feature/i); }); }

request.description: Deliberately invalid body so the feature gate is observable without starting a restore: 403 (FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_RESTORE off) vs 400 (on). checkFeature precedes parseAndValidateRestoreRequest in restorePush.

pm.test('SKIPPED - set other_partition_id (a second onboarded partition) to exercise CON-02', function () { pm.expect(true).to.be.true; });

item.name: TC-RST-FUNC-01/02 - poll status until Succeeded

exec: // Wait between polls (10s by default) so we don't hammer the status endpoint. Skips the delay on the first poll.
// Stop polling on an unexpected status code - don't burn retries; fall through to the next request.
var j = {}; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {}
if (status === 'Succeeded') { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', '0'); pm.test('RST-003 restore Succeeded', function () { pm.expect(status).to.eql('Succeeded'); }); }
else if (status === 'Failed') { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', '0'); pm.expect.fail('Restore Failed: ' + (j.error_message || j.error || 'no detail')); }

else if (status === 'Rejected') { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', '0'); pm.test('restore did not end Rejected (Rejected is unexpected for this scenario)', function () { pm.expect(status, (j.error_message || j.error || j.message || j.statusMessage || pm.response.text() || 'no detail')).to.not.eql('Rejected'); }); }

else { if (attempt < maxAttempts) { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', String(attempt + 1)); pm.execution.setNextRequest(pm.info.requestName); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set('poll_attempt', '0'); pm.expect.fail('Not terminal within ' + maxAttempts + ' polls (last: ' + status + ')'); } }

request.description: Poll to terminal. Succeeded satisfies RST-003 for the functional restore. Set a per-request delay (~poll_delay_ms) in the runner.

request.description: METADATA assertion for TC-RST-FUNC-01/02: after restore succeeds, filemetadata.totalSize must have reverted from the post-update v2 value (49) back to the pre-update v1 baseline (16). Blob-data (byte-level) verification follows in the next two requests.
